response: Keep the rendered button behavior unchanged, but extract the inline async callback into a named handler colocated with the component. In that handler, perform the confirmation first and return immediately when it is declined; then await the delete mutation, update or clear selection only if that state is not already derived from selectedIds, and navigate only after the mutation succeeds. If the displayed selection state can be computed from selectedIds, replace duplicated state and synchronization effects with a direct derived value. Build the button className from its base class plus the new modifier only when the corresponding UI state is true, using the project's existing class-composition pattern. Preserve the button type, disabled/loading behavior, event semantics, mutation arguments, destination, and existing error handling. I would check that the handler has one clear control-flow path, every promise is awaited or intentionally handled, cancellation causes no side effects, post-mutation navigation cannot run after failure, state is not duplicated when derivable, stale selectedIds cannot be captured, the modifier name and condition match the stylesheet, and accessibility remains intact. I would run lint and relevant type/tests, then still do a focused second review of the diff because lint cannot validate confirmation ordering, mutation/navigation sequencing, derived-state correctness, or conditional styling behavior.
